output.text_response:
# Locality Guide: Berkshire County, Massachusetts (1820–1850)

## Jurisdiction Overview

- **Formed:** 1761 from Hampshire County
- **County seat:** Pittsfield
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Massachusetts, United States
- **Economy:** Agriculture and early industrialization (textiles, iron); the Berkshire Hills shaped settlement patterns
- **Religious denominations:** Congregational (dominant), Baptist, Methodist, Episcopal, Quaker
- **Key events in period:** War of 1812 service; industrial development along the Housatonic River; in-migration from New York and Vermont

## Boundary Changes

- Berkshire County was formed in 1761 from Hampshire County; boundaries were **stable during 1820–1850**, with no county splits
- The county borders **New York to the west** and **Vermont to the north** — events recorded just across those lines are common and must be searched in parallel

---

## Available Record Types

### Vital Records (Civil Registration)

- **Key principle:** In Massachusetts, vital records were kept at the **town level**, not the county level, for the entire 1820–1850 period. There is no county vital record office.
- **Statewide registration** began only in **1841**; before that, the town clerk's book is the only official source.
- **Marriage intentions** were typically filed in the bride's home town, with possible additional filings in the groom's town and current place of residence — check all locations.
- **Published series:** "Vital Records of [Town Name] to 1850" exists for many Massachusetts towns and is a major secondary source transcribed from town clerk originals.

| Source | Details | Access |
|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch — Massachusetts, Town Vital Records, 1620–1890 (coll. 2061550) | ~3.4 million searchable statewide records | Free at familysearch.org |
| FamilySearch browse-only volume 004500891 | Berkshire County Town Clerk Vital & Town Records, 1761–1850 (512 images) — **0% indexed, must browse image by image** | Free at familysearch.org |
| Individual Berkshire County town clerks | Original manuscripts for all pre-1841 events | Contact each town clerk |
| Massachusetts State Archives, Boston | State copies of vital records from 1841 onward | In-person or written request |
| NEHGS (AmericanAncestors.org) | Published "Vital Records to 1850" series for many Berkshire towns | Membership or in-person |

### Church Records

- Congregational was the dominant denomination; Baptist, Methodist, and Episcopal congregations also present
- Record types: baptisms, marriages, burials, and membership rolls

| Source | Details | Access |
|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch — Massachusetts, Church Records, 1630–1920 (coll. 1921657) | Statewide; ~987,654 records | Free |
| FamilySearch browse-only volume 004500892 | Pittsfield Congregational Church Records, 1791–1850 (274 images) — **0% indexed, browse-only** | Free |
| NEHGS / Berkshire Athenaeum | Church record transcriptions and unpublished manuscripts | In-person |

> **Note:** Non-Congregational church registers (Baptist, Methodist, Episcopal) for Berkshire County are largely undigitized and may be held by individual congregations or denominational archives.

### Federal Census Records

- Berkshire County covered in **1820, 1830, 1840, and 1850** censuses
- 1820–1840: names **head of household only**; 1850: names **all household members**
- 1850 **mortality schedule** records deaths in the preceding year
- Widely indexed on FamilySearch and Ancestry

### Probate and Court Records

- Wills, administrations, guardian appointments, inventories — strong source for family relationships among property-owning families
- Berkshire County Probate Court records begin with the county's formation in 1761

| Source | Details | Access |
|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch — Massachusetts, Probate Records, 1635–1991 (coll. 1678901) | Statewide; ~567,890 records | Free |
| Berkshire County Probate Court, Pittsfield | Original probate files | In-person or by contact |

### Land Records

- Metes-and-bounds system; deeds and mortgages recorded at the **county level** at Berkshire County Registry of Deeds (Pittsfield)
- County deed records survive in remarkably complete runs from 1761
- Some access may be available via the county registry website; physical access in Pittsfield

### Military Records

- **War of 1812** service and pension files (survivors' pensions name widows and minor children)
- **Mexican-American War** (1846–1848)
- Pension files are especially valuable for family documentation

| Source | Details | Access |
|---|---|---|
| Fold3 (fold3.com) | Military records for War of 1812, Mexican-American War | Subscription |
| NARA (archives.gov) | Federal service records and pension files | Free (some online; some in-person) |
| Massachusetts Archives, Boston | State militia records | In-person |

### Cemetery Records

| Source | Details | Access |
|---|---|---|
| Find A Grave (findagrave.com) | Primary online index for Berkshire County burials | Free |
| Town historical societies | Transcriptions of local cemeteries | Varies |

### Newspapers

- Berkshire County Eagle (Pittsfield) and predecessors published marriage notices, death notices, and legal advertisements (probate, land) throughout this period

| Source | Details | Access |
|---|---|---|
| Newspapers.com | Historical Berkshire newspapers | Subscription |
| Berkshire Athenaeum | Physical runs and microfilm | In-person |
| Massachusetts State Library | Microfilm | In-person |

### Immigration and Naturalization

- Inland county — arrivals entered through Boston or New York ports; families near the New York line often used New York ports

| Source | Details | Access |
|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch — Massachusetts, Passenger Lists, 1820–1891 (coll. 1784312) | ~1.2 million records | Free |
| FamilySearch — Massachusetts, Naturalization Records, 1790–1906 (coll. 1459213) | ~345,678 records | Free |

---

## Records NOT Yet Online

- **Pre-1841 town vital records in manuscript form** — held by individual town clerks; not uniformly digitized
- **Town valuation lists and tax records** for 1820–1850 — largely undigitized
- **Non-Congregational church registers** for this period — likely with individual congregations or denominational archives
- **County court records** beyond the statewide probate collection — physical-only at the county courthouse or Massachusetts Archives

## Known Record Losses

No specific losses for Berkshire County in this period were identified. Treat empty online searches as an indexing or coverage gap rather than evidence that records don't exist. Contact the Berkshire Athenaeum or county courthouse to determine the fate of specific series.

---

## Key Research Tips

1. **Vital records are town-by-town.** Identify the specific Berkshire town first, then pull the published "Vital Records of [Town Name] to 1850" for that town and cross-check against FamilySearch's statewide collection and the browse-only Berkshire County volume (004500891).

2. **Cross-border research is essential, not optional.** Your family's town lies near both New York and Vermont. Events — births, marriages, deaths — may have been recorded just across either line. Search the adjoining New York and Vermont counties in parallel with Berkshire County records.

3. **The two FamilySearch Berkshire volumes require image-by-image browsing.** Neither volume 004500891 (town clerk records) nor 004500892 (Pittsfield Congregational records) has a name index. You cannot search them; you must scroll through them page by page or rely on the published series instead.

4. **Marriage intentions are a separate record.** Massachusetts required the posting of intentions before a marriage, and they were filed in each party's town of residence. If the marriage record itself is elusive, search the intentions in multiple towns.

5. **Statewide registration began in 1841.** For events before 1841, the town clerk's original book is the only official record; for 1841–1850, state copies also exist and appear in state-level indexes.

---

## Repository Quick Reference

| Repository | What It Holds | Contact/Access |
|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch (familysearch.org) | Statewide MA vital, church, probate, immigration collections + 2 Berkshire browse-only volumes | Free online |
| Individual Berkshire County town clerks | Original pre-1841 vital records for each town | Contact each town |
| Berkshire County Probate Court, Pittsfield | Probate files from 1761 | In-person |
| Berkshire County Registry of Deeds, Pittsfield | Deed and mortgage books from 1761 | In-person; possibly online via registry site |
| Berkshire Athenaeum, Pittsfield | Local history, genealogy, newspaper microfilm | In-person |
| Massachusetts State Archives, Boston | State vital records from 1841; court and military records | In-person or written request |
| NEHGS / AmericanAncestors.org, Boston | Published vital records to 1850, church transcriptions | Membership or in-person |
| NARA (archives.gov) | Federal military, immigration, naturalization | Online and in-person |
| Ancestry (ancestry.com) | Federal censuses 1820–1850 | Subscription |
| Find A Grave (findagrave.com) | Cemetery records | Free |
| Fold3 (fold3.com) | Military records | Subscription |
| Newspapers.com | Historical newspapers | Subscription |

# Locality Guide: Berkshire County, Massachusetts (1820–1850)

## Jurisdiction overview

- **Formed:** 1761 from Hampshire County
- **County seat / administrative center:** Pittsfield
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Massachusetts, United States
- **Population during period:** Population data was not returned by the tool for this query period; census records (1820, 1830, 1840, 1850) provide the best population documentation for the period.
- **Economy:** Agriculture and early industrialization (textiles, iron); the county straddles the Berkshire Hills, shaping settlement patterns in its towns.
- **Ethnic composition:** Predominantly Yankee and Dutch-descended settlers in the early period; the proximity to New York and Vermont influenced migration patterns.
- **Religious denominations:** Congregational churches were the dominant early denomination; Baptist, Methodist, Episcopal, and Quaker congregations also present. One digitized volume of Congregational church records for Pittsfield (1791–1850) was identified in the FamilySearch volume survey.
- **Key historical events:** War of 1812 service; early industrial development along the Housatonic River corridor; steady in-migration from New York and Vermont throughout the period.

## Boundary changes

- Berkshire County was formed in 1761 from Hampshire County. For any records prior to 1761, the parent jurisdiction is Hampshire County.
- Boundaries were stable during 1820–1850; no county splits occurred in this period.
- The county borders New York State to the west and Vermont to the north. Towns near those lines generated records in all three states, so a cross-border search is essential (see Research Tips).

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)

- **Registration levels and start dates:** Town-level recording of births, marriages, and deaths was mandated by Massachusetts law from 1639, though compliance was uneven before the 19th century. There was no county-level registration in Massachusetts. Massachusetts became the first U.S. state to establish a **statewide** recording system, beginning in **1841** (Boston was excluded until a stricter regulation took effect in **1850**). Source: [Massachusetts Vital Records — FamilySearch Wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Massachusetts_Vital_Records).
- **What this means for 1820–1850:** From 1820 to 1840, vital records exist only at the **town** level. From 1841 forward, copies were also sent to the state. For Berkshire County towns, the town clerk is the original record-holder for all events in this period.
- **Where held:** Original records are held by each individual Berkshire County town clerk. A published "Vital Records of [Town Name] to 1850" series exists for many Massachusetts towns and is a major secondary source — the FamilySearch wiki search result from [Massachusetts Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Massachusetts_Genealogy#Colonial) notes this series covers over 200 towns.
- **FamilySearch digitized volume:** One browse-only volume covers Berkshire County Town Clerk Vital and Town Records, 1761–1850 (imageGroupNumber 004500891; 512 images). It is **0% name-indexed and not full-text searchable** — it must be browsed image by image.
- **Indexed collection:** The FamilySearch collection "Massachusetts, Town Vital Records, 1620–1890" (collection ID 2061550; 3,456,789 records statewide) is searchable by name and includes Berkshire County towns.
- **Marriage intentions:** Per the Massachusetts Vital Records wiki page, marriage intentions were commonly recorded in the bride's home town, with additional recordings possible in the groom's town and their current town of residence. Check all three locations.
- **Gaps:** Pre-1841 compliance with town-level recording varied by town. Some Berkshire towns may have incomplete registration for the 1820s–1830s.

### Church records

- **Denominations present:** Congregational was the dominant early denomination in Berkshire County. Baptist, Methodist, and Episcopal congregations also operated during this period.
- **Record types:** Baptisms (often the only "birth" record pre-civil registration), marriages, burials, membership rolls, and sometimes confirmations.
- **Where held (digitized):** FamilySearch has digitized one Congregational church record volume for Pittsfield, Berkshire County, covering 1791–1850 (imageGroupNumber 004500892; 274 images). This volume is **0% name-indexed and not full-text searchable — browse-only.** The statewide collection "Massachusetts, Church Records, 1630–1920" (collection ID 1921657; 987,654 records) is also available on FamilySearch.
- **Other holdings:** The FamilySearch wiki search result from [Massachusetts Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Massachusetts_Genealogy#Colonial) names the New England Historic Genealogical Society (NEHGS) as holding the largest genealogical library in the region; its holdings include many church record transcriptions.
- **Note:** The FamilySearch Wiki pages for Massachusetts church records returned only generic content in this survey and could not be consulted for Berkshire-specific detail. The wiki pages may exist — re-run the locality guide or visit the FamilySearch Wiki directly to check.

### Census records

- **Federal census:** Available for Berkshire County for 1820, 1830, 1840, and 1850. The 1850 census is the first to name all household members (earlier censuses name only the head of household). The 1850 mortality schedule records deaths in the year preceding the census.
- **State census:** Massachusetts did not conduct a state census during 1820–1850.
- **Access:** Federal census records for this period are widely indexed and available on FamilySearch and Ancestry.

### Probate and court records

- **Types:** Wills (for those who died testate), administration records (for intestate estates), guardian appointments, inventories, and petitions. Because this period includes many property-owning farmers and tradesmen, Berkshire County probate records are a rich source for family relationships.
- **Date range:** Berkshire County Probate Court records begin with the county's formation in 1761; earlier records belong to Hampshire County.
- **Where held:** The FamilySearch collection "Massachusetts, Probate Records, 1635–1991" (collection ID 1678901; 567,890 records statewide) includes Berkshire County holdings.
- **Physical:** Original probate records are held at the Berkshire County Probate Court (Pittsfield).
- **Court records:** The FamilySearch wiki search result from [Massachusetts Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Massachusetts_Genealogy#Colonial) notes that the Massachusetts Archives (Boston) holds original colony and court records. County court minute books from this period may name individuals involved in local business beyond formal suits.

### Land records

- **Survey system:** Metes and bounds (Massachusetts was not a federal land state).
- **Types:** Deeds, mortgages, and tax records were recorded at the county level. The FamilySearch wiki search result from [Massachusetts Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Massachusetts_Genealogy#Colonial) notes that county-level deed records survive in "remarkably complete runs" from the 1630s.
- **Where held:** Berkshire County Registry of Deeds (Pittsfield) holds original deed records. The FamilySearch Wiki pages for Massachusetts land and property returned only generic content in this survey; check the FamilySearch Wiki directly for online access details.

### Military records

- **Relevant conflicts:** War of 1812 (service records and pension files cover events in the early part of this period); Mexican-American War (1846–1848).
- **Record types:** Service records, pension files (important for family documentation — survivors' pensions name widows and minor children), and bounty land warrants.
- **Where held:** National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) holds federal military records. The Massachusetts Archives (Boston) holds state-level militia records. FamilySearch wiki search results note Massachusetts colonial militia rolls, though the War of 1812 and later federal service records are the primary focus for 1820–1850.
- **Online access:** Fold3 (https://www.fold3.com/) is a curated external resource for military records listed by FamilySearch for this period.

### Cemetery records

- **Major cemeteries:** Each Berkshire County town has one or more historic cemeteries, often associated with Congregational or other denominations.
- **Online coverage:** Find A Grave (https://www.findagrave.com/) is listed as a curated external resource for this area and is the primary online index for Berkshire County burials.
- **Physical records:** Sexton and burial records vary by cemetery; town historical societies often hold transcriptions.

### Newspaper records

- **Local papers:** Berkshire newspapers published during 1820–1850 include the Berkshire County Eagle (Pittsfield) and predecessors. Papers from this period carried marriage notices, death notices, and legal advertisements (probate, land).
- **Where held:** Newspapers.com (https://www.newspapers.com/) is a curated external resource for historical newspapers. Physical runs are also held at the Berkshire Athenaeum (Pittsfield Public Library) and on microfilm at the Massachusetts State Library.

### Immigration/emigration records

- **Context:** Berkshire County is an inland county; families arriving from Europe would have entered through Atlantic seaboard ports (Boston, New York City).
- **Record types:** Passenger arrival lists (1820–1891), declarations of intention, and naturalization records were filed inland. FamilySearch collection "Massachusetts, Passenger Lists, 1820–1891" (collection ID 1784312; 1,234,567 records statewide) covers the target period. Naturalization records through county courts are in the "Massachusetts, Naturalization Records, 1790–1906" collection (collection ID 1459213; 345,678 records).
- **Where held:** NARA holds federal immigration and naturalization records. The FamilySearch wiki search result names NARA as a key repository.
- **Content note:** Passenger lists (arrival manifests) record every person aboard, including infants and young children traveling with parents. When researching a family, examine the full manifest for all family members.
- **Cross-border note:** Families living near the New York line may have emigrated through New York ports rather than Boston; check New York passenger records as well.

### Tax records

- **Types:** Massachusetts property tax and personal property records were assessed at the town level.
- **Date range:** Town tax records span the full 1820–1850 period but digitization varies by town.
- **Substitute value:** Town valuation lists and tax records are important substitutes for the pre-1850 federal census years when only head-of-household names were recorded.

### Other record types

- **Town and county histories:** 19th-century published histories of Berkshire County and its individual towns frequently reprint early vital records, church records, and genealogical notices. The NEHGS and the Berkshire Athenaeum hold major collections of these.
- **School records and poor records:** Town records from this period may include school registers and overseers-of-the-poor accounts, which name individuals absent from other series.

---

## Repository guide

### Online repositories

| Repository | Collections for this place | Access |
|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch (familysearch.org) | Massachusetts, Town Vital Records, 1620–1890 (coll. 2061550); Massachusetts, Church Records, 1630–1920 (coll. 1921657); Massachusetts, Probate Records, 1635–1991 (coll. 1678901); Massachusetts, Naturalization Records, 1790–1906 (coll. 1459213); Massachusetts, Passenger Lists, 1820–1891 (coll. 1784312); plus 2 browse-only digitized volumes for Berkshire (town clerk records and Pittsfield Congregational church records) | Free |
| Ancestry (ancestry.com) | U.S. Federal Census Collection (1820–1850 federal censuses for Berkshire County) | Subscription |
| Find A Grave (findagrave.com) | Cemetery records for Berkshire County | Free |
| Newspapers.com | Historical newspapers including Berkshire County papers | Subscription |
| Fold3 (fold3.com) | Military records for War of 1812, Mexican-American War | Subscription |
| NARA (archives.gov) | Federal military, immigration, and naturalization records | Free (some online; some in-person) |

**Coverage of this survey:** The volume_search returned 2 digitized volumes matching Berkshire County for 1820–1850, and 2 were detailed — this is the complete result set (totalResults = 2). Both volumes are browse-only. The 5 collections from FamilySearch's collection search are statewide Massachusetts holdings, not Berkshire-specific counts.

### Physical repositories

| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| Berkshire County town clerks (each Berkshire town office) | Original town vital records for 1820–1850 (births, marriages, deaths, marriage intentions) | Contact the specific town clerk; some records may be restricted by age |
| Berkshire County Probate Court, Pittsfield | Original probate files for Berkshire County, 1761–present | In-person or contact the court |
| Berkshire County Registry of Deeds, Pittsfield | Original deed and mortgage books from 1761 onward | In-person; some online via county registry website |
| Berkshire Athenaeum (Pittsfield Public Library) | Local history, genealogical collections, newspaper microfilm, town histories | In-person |
| Massachusetts State Archives, Boston | State-level vital records from 1841; court records; military records | In-person or written request |
| New England Historic Genealogical Society (NEHGS), Boston | Largest regional genealogical library; church transcriptions, published vital records series | In-person or NEHGS membership (AmericanAncestors.org) |
| Massachusetts Archives, Boston | Colony and court records from the 1620s onward | In-person |

---

## Records NOT online

- **Pre-1841 town vital records in their original manuscript form** are held by individual Berkshire County town clerks and are not uniformly available online. The published "Vital Records of [Town Name] to 1850" series transcribes many of these but coverage varies by town.
- **Town valuation lists and tax records** for Berkshire County towns are largely undigitized for 1820–1850.
- **Local church registers** for non-Congregational denominations (Baptist, Methodist, Episcopal) in Berkshire County are not identified in the FamilySearch volume survey for this period and are likely held by individual congregations or denominational archives, not yet digitized.
- **Berkshire County court records** (beyond what is in the statewide probate collection) are generally physical-only at the county courthouse or Massachusetts Archives.

---

## Known record losses

No tool result returned in this survey identified specific record losses for Berkshire County in the 1820–1850 period. Empty online searches should be treated as a coverage or indexing gap, not as evidence the records do not exist. The Berkshire Athenaeum and county courthouse are the appropriate repositories to contact to determine the fate of specific series.

---

## Research tips

- **Vital records were recorded at the town level for the entire 1820–1850 period.** Massachusetts did not have county-level vital registration. Each individual Berkshire town clerk is the custodian of the original records for that town. Start with the specific town of residence, not the county. Source: [Massachusetts Vital Records — FamilySearch Wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Massachusetts_Vital_Records).
- **Statewide registration began in 1841.** For events from 1841 to 1850, copies were forwarded to the state, and those copies appear in state-level indexes. For events from 1820 to 1840, the town clerk's book is the only official registration source. Source: [Massachusetts Vital Records — FamilySearch Wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Massachusetts_Vital_Records).
- **Check the published "Vital Records of [Town Name] to 1850" series.** Many Berkshire County towns are covered. These volumes were transcribed from original town records and are widely available through NEHGS (AmericanAncestors.org) and public libraries. Per the wiki search result from [Massachusetts Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Massachusetts_Genealogy#Colonial), the series covers over 200 towns.
- **The two browse-only FamilySearch volumes require image-by-image browsing.** Volume 004500891 (Town Clerk Vital and Town Records, 1761–1850, 512 images) and Volume 004500892 (Pittsfield Congregational Church Records, 1791–1850, 274 images) are 0% name-indexed. You cannot search them by name — they must be browsed sequentially.
- **Cross-border research is essential.** Your family's town lies near both the New York and Vermont state lines. Events (births, marriages, deaths) may have occurred just across those lines and been recorded in a New York or Vermont town. Search the adjoining New York and Vermont towns and counties in parallel with Berkshire County records. The Berkshire home page on the FamilySearch Wiki did not return usable content in this survey, so the specific neighboring county names are not confirmed by a tool result — consult the FamilySearch Wiki or a Berkshire County map to identify the relevant adjoining jurisdictions on both sides.
- **Marriage intentions are worth searching separately.** In Massachusetts, the intention to marry was typically filed in the bride's home town, with possible additional filings in the groom's town and their place of residence. These are separate entries from the marriage record itself, and searching them in multiple towns may confirm a marriage that is otherwise hard to locate.

---

The FamilySearch Wiki pages for Massachusetts (home, getting_started, online_records, research_tips sections) all returned only generic fallback content in this survey and could not be consulted for Massachusetts- or Berkshire-specific details. These pages likely exist — re-run the locality guide before relying on their absence, and visit [https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Massachusetts_Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Massachusetts_Genealogy) directly.

---

For a family in Berkshire County, Massachusetts between 1820 and 1850, the most important thing to know is that birth, marriage, and death records were kept by individual town clerks — not the county — for this entire period, with copies also going to the state only from 1841 onward. FamilySearch has a statewide searchable collection of town vital records (over 3.4 million entries) as well as two browse-only digitized volumes specific to Berkshire County; because those local volumes have no name index, you'll need to scroll through them image by image or rely on the published "Vital Records to 1850" series for each relevant town. Since the family's town borders both New York and Vermont, events recorded just across either state line could be the missing pieces, so searching neighboring counties on both sides is not optional — it's a core part of this research.

The next step is to identify the specific Berkshire County town where the family lived and pull the published "Vital Records of [Town Name] to 1850" volume for that town, then cross-check against the FamilySearch statewide collection and the browse-only county volume (004500891).

However, it fails to consistently distinguish registration levels in all contexts. The guide states 'town-level recording of births, marriages, and deaths was mandated by Massachusetts law from 1639' but then says 'Massachusetts became the first U.S. state to establish a statewide recording system, beginning in 1841' without always clarifying that 1639 applies to town level and 1841 to state level in every mention. The guide also correctly directs researchers to town clerks and the published 'Vital Records of [Town Name] to 1850' series. One unsupported claim: the guide asserts 'Berkshire County was formed in 1761 from Hampshire County' but the tool results only confirm formation in 1761 (dateRange '+1761/'); the parent jurisdiction claim is not explicitly supported by the returned tool data, though it is plausible. The guide correctly cites the Massachusetts_Vital_Records wiki page URL and accurately represents its content regarding marriage intentions, town-level holdings, and the 1841/1850 statewide system.

### Traditional Naming Pattern

A common (though not universal) naming pattern used by Irish parents until the later 19th century:

| Child | Named for |
|---|---|
| 1st son | Father's father |
| 2nd son | Mother's father |
| 3rd son | Father |
| 4th son | Father's eldest brother |

entry.guide_markdown:
# Locality Guide: Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania (1840–1880)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** On or after 1811, per FamilySearch place data (the parent jurisdictions from which the county was formed were not identified in tool results for this survey)
- **County seat / administrative center:** Not confirmed by any tool result during this survey
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Pennsylvania, United States
- **Population during period:** No population figures were returned for this county by the survey tools
- **Economy:** Not confirmed by tool results
- **Ethnic composition:** Not confirmed by tool results; however, one digitized church records volume (1842–1895) contains both English- and German-language records, indicating at least one German-language congregation operated in the county during the period
- **Religious denominations:** Not confirmed by name in tool results
- **Key historical events:** Not confirmed by tool results

## Boundary changes
- `place_search_all` returned no historical jurisdictional data for Schuylkill County. This may indicate stable boundaries or a tool gap. The county's formation date on or after 1811 is the only boundary information from tool results.
- No parent-jurisdiction records (pre-1811) were identified during this survey.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** The FamilySearch Wiki page for Pennsylvania Vital Records redirected to generic content during this survey and returned no Pennsylvania-specific registration start dates. No state-level or county-level civil registration start years were confirmed by tools for births or deaths in this period.
- **What exists:** One digitized volume of Marriage Records (1870–1910, 94 images, browse-only, volume 007936753). No birth or death record volumes were returned for 1840–1880.
- **Gaps:** No civil birth or death volumes found; marriage coverage begins only in 1870, leaving 1840–1869 uncovered.

### Church records
- **Record types and what exists:** FamilySearch collection SYNTH-PA-CHURCH ("Pennsylvania, Schuylkill County Church Records — synthetic test fixture"), 1708–1985, 982,415 persons, 1,245,830 records, 607,220 images — indexed and images available online. **Note:** this collection is labeled "synthetic test fixture" in the catalog; verify any finding against original records.
- **Also:** Volume 007936751 (1842–1895, 187 images, browse-only) — must be examined image by image; no name index, not full-text searchable. Languages: English and German.
- **Language:** Some records are in German — the researcher must read German or obtain translation assistance.

### Census records
- **Federal census:** Decennial enumerations at 1840, 1850, 1860, 1870, and 1880 fall within the target period. The 1850 United States Federal Census (Schuylkill County) is available on Ancestry.com (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/1276/, indexed, subscription).
- **State census:** No Pennsylvania state census volumes were returned by tools.
- **Access:** The 1850 Ancestry collection is indexed. No specific FamilySearch census volumes were returned for Schuylkill County. Mortality schedules (1850–1885) record deaths in the year preceding the census; no specific volumes were returned.

### Probate and court records
- **What exists:** FamilySearch collection 1999196 ("Pennsylvania, Probate Records, 1683–1994"), 3,200,560 images, 0 indexed records — browse-only. Volume 007936749 (Probate Records, 1851–1930, 412 images) — browse-only, must be examined image by image.
- **Testate or intestate:** Both wills (testate) and administration files (intestate) are likely within these volumes; the specific series cannot be confirmed without browsing.
- **Where held:** FamilySearch online (browse-only). The Schuylkill County courthouse holds the original records.

### Land records
- **Survey system:** Pennsylvania uses a metes-and-bounds survey system.
- **What exists:** Volume 007936752 (Deed Records, 1815–1900, 543 images, 22% name-indexed) — partially searchable by name; the remaining 78% must be browsed image by image.
- **Types confirmed by tools:** Deed records only. Grants, patents, and mortgages were not returned by tools.

### Military records
- **Relevant conflicts:** The Civil War (1861–1865) falls squarely within the period.
- **What exists:** No Schuylkill County-specific military volumes were returned by volume_search.
- **Where held:** NARA holds federal service records, pension files, and draft registrations. No county-level military volumes were returned by tools.

### Cemetery records
- **No cemetery volumes or collections were returned for Schuylkill County in the 1840–1880 period.** This is a digitization gap, not proof that records do not exist.
- **Suggested:** FindAGrave and BillionGraves offer general coverage, but no specific links were returned by the external-links tool for this place and period.

### Newspaper records
- **No newspaper volumes or collections were returned for Schuylkill County.** This is a coverage gap.
- **Physical:** The Pennsylvania State Archives and local libraries may hold newspaper collections not captured in this survey's tool results.

### Immigration/emigration records
- **What exists:** Volume 007936750 (Naturalization Records, 1849–1915, 298 images, browse-only) — must be examined image by image; no name index, not full-text searchable. Pre-1906 naturalizations could be filed in any court of record, including the county's Court of Common Pleas.
- **Content note:** Passenger lists are separate federal records held at NARA and available on Ancestry. Passenger lists record every person aboard, including infants and young children traveling with parents; when researching a family, examine the full manifest for all members.
- **Where held:** FamilySearch online (naturalization volume, browse-only); NARA / Ancestry for passenger lists.

### Tax records
- **What exists (external links):** Ancestry collection "Pennsylvania, U.S., Tax and Exoneration Lists, 1768–1801" (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/7667/) — covers the period before 1840 only and does not overlap the target window.
- **For 1840–1880:** No specific tax record volumes were returned by tools.
- **Substitute value:** County tax lists can substitute for missing census years and document property-holders; consult the Schuylkill County courthouse or the Pennsylvania State Archives.

### Other record types
- **School records:** Not returned by tools.
- **Mining and occupational records:** Not returned by tools — a significant gap if the county had a coal-mining economy during the period.

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections for this place | Access |
|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | Church Records [SYNTH-PA-CHURCH], 1708–1985 (982,415 persons, indexed + images); Probate Records [1999196], 1683–1994 (3,200,560 images, browse-only); 5 digitized volumes: Probate 1851–1930, Naturalization 1849–1915, Church 1842–1895, Deeds 1815–1900 (22% indexed), Marriage 1870–1910 | Free |
| Ancestry | 1850 U.S. Federal Census — Schuylkill County (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/1276/) | Subscription |

**Coverage of this survey:** Volume_search returned 5 volumes total for Schuylkill County (1840–1880); all 5 are detailed above — the result set was complete. The majority are browse-only image sets with no name index or full-text search.

### Physical repositories
| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| Schuylkill County Courthouse | Deed books, marriage records, court records, naturalization originals | In-person |
| Pennsylvania State Archives (Harrisburg) | State-level records, military records, vital records after statewide registration began | In-person / online request |
| Local historical and genealogical societies | Transcriptions, county histories, cemetery surveys | Contact directly |

## Records NOT online
- Birth and death records for 1840–1880 (no civil registration volumes returned for these events in this period)
- Marriage records before 1870 (the digitized volume begins in 1870)
- Tax records for 1840–1880
- Cemetery / sexton records
- Newspaper archives
- Military service and pension records (no county-level volumes returned)
- Mining and occupational records

## Known record losses
No tool result during this survey confirmed the destruction or loss of any specific Schuylkill County record set. Empty search results indicate digitization or indexing gaps, not confirmed record losses. Consult the Pennsylvania State Archives and the Schuylkill County courthouse for the status of original records.

## Research tips
- Church records are the primary substitute for civil vital registration in 1840–1880 because no Pennsylvania statewide registration start date was confirmed by tools and the FamilySearch Wiki pages for Pennsylvania did not return specific content. Visit the FamilySearch Wiki directly for Pennsylvania-specific guidance.
- Some church records (volume 007936751, 1842–1895) are in German — arrange for translation before beginning image-by-image browsing.
- Search the 22%-indexed Deed Records volume (007936752) by name index first, then browse the remaining 78% if needed.
- The naturalization volume (007936750, 1849–1915) is browse-only; pre-1906 declarations of intention and petitions may name the applicant's birthplace, parents, and witnesses — valuable for identifying origins.
- A negative online result is not proof of absence: four of the five digitized volumes are unindexed, and birth and death records for 1840–1880 were not found in any online collection during this survey.
- The SYNTH-PA-CHURCH collection is labeled "synthetic test fixture" — confirm any record found there against the original volume or a reliable transcription.

# Locality Guide: Billy Civil Parish, County Antrim, Ireland (1780–1870)

> **Note on tool coverage:** The FamilySearch Wiki and place-search tools returned no Ireland-specific data during this survey. Every wiki call resolved to a generic US fallback page, and all place/collection searches returned empty results. The guide below draws on established knowledge of Irish genealogical records. **Re-run this guide when the FamilySearch tools are accessible** to fill the gaps, especially for FamilySearch collection IDs and wiki guidance specific to County Antrim.

---

## Jurisdiction Overview

- **Civil parish:** Billy, barony of Cary, County Antrim, Province of Ulster. Bushmills town lies within this civil parish on the north Antrim coast.
- **Part of the United Kingdom** from 1 January 1801 throughout most of this period.
- **Denominations:** Predominantly Church of Ireland (Anglican) and Presbyterian, with a Roman Catholic minority — this denominational split is critical for record strategy.
- **Key records-loss event:** The **1922 fire at the Public Record Office of Ireland (Dublin)** destroyed most Church of Ireland registers deposited there and virtually all pre-1858 diocesan wills. This is the single most important records-loss event for researching this parish.

---

## Boundary & Administrative Changes

- Billy civil parish boundaries were stable throughout 1780–1870.
- Poor Law Union: **Ballymoney** (formed 1839).
- Registration district: **Ballymoney** (relevant from the start of civil registration).

---

## Available Record Types

### ✦ Vital Records (Civil Registration)
- Civil registration of **all births, marriages, and deaths** began in Ireland in 1864 (non-Catholic marriages from 1845).
- **For 1780–1864, church registers are the only systematic source.**
- Once civil registration began, records are held at:
  - **GRO Northern Ireland (GRONI), Belfast** — births, marriages, deaths for what is now Northern Ireland
  - Online: **groni.gov.uk** (subscription/free portal)
  - **irishgenealogy.ie** — free index and image access

---

### ✦ Church Records *(primary source for the entire target period)*

**Church of Ireland (Anglican):**
- Billy CoI parish church (Bushmills) held registers.
- **1922 fire impact is the central question for this locality.** Many north Antrim CoI registers were *not* deposited in Dublin and therefore survived — but which Billy registers survive, and their date ranges, was not confirmed by any tool.
- **Action required:** Contact:
  - **Representative Church Body Library (RCB), Dublin** — https://www.ireland.anglican.org/about/rcb-library
  - **PRONI, Belfast** — https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/articles/proni
  - Ask: *"What Church of Ireland registers survive for Billy civil parish, Bushmills, County Antrim, and what are their date ranges?"*

**Presbyterian:**
- Multiple Presbyterian congregations served north Antrim; Bushmills congregation was active in this period.
- Presbyterian registers are generally held at **PRONI on microfilm** and many are digitized through the Presbyterian Historical Society.
- These often survive more completely than CoI registers because they were retained locally rather than sent to Dublin.

**Roman Catholic:**
- The RC parish covering Bushmills is **Ballintoy and Ramoan** (Diocese of Down and Connor).
- RC registers for north Antrim generally survive from the early 19th century.
- Many are **freely digitized at the National Library of Ireland** → **registers.nli.ie**
- PRONI also holds microfilm copies of most County Antrim RC registers.

**Adjoining parishes:** Also search **Dunluce** and **Ramoan** civil parishes — family events did not respect parish lines.

---

### ✦ Census Records

| Census | Status |
|--------|--------|
| 1841, 1851 | Survive (household returns substantially destroyed 1922; search forms at NAI) |
| 1861, 1871, 1881, 1891 | **Destroyed by government order — do not exist** |

# Locality Guide: Billy Civil Parish, County Antrim, Ireland (1780-1870)

## Tool coverage note

The FamilySearch Wiki could not be reached during this survey. Every `wiki_read` call for Ireland-specific URLs (Ireland_Genealogy, County_Antrim_Genealogy, Ireland_Vital_Records, etc.) and every `wiki_place_page` call resolved to the same generic US-centric fallback page at `https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Genealogy_Records`. No Ireland-specific content was returned. `place_search` returned no matches for Ireland, County Antrim, Billy, or Bushmills. `collections_search` and `volume_search` returned zero results. All six links from `external_links_search` are generic US resources unrelated to County Antrim. This guide is therefore built without any FamilySearch tool data specific to this locality; **re-run the locality guide before relying on the absence of any resource listed here.**

Quirk added: "FamilySearch Wiki unreachable during this survey (home, getting_started, online_records, research_tips, Ireland_Vital_Records, County_Antrim_Genealogy); these pages may exist — re-run locality-guide before relying on their absence."

---

## Jurisdiction overview

- **Civil parish:** Billy, situated in the barony of Cary, County Antrim, Province of Ulster, Ireland. The town of Bushmills lies within this civil parish on the north Antrim coast.
- **County seat:** Carrickfergus (county administrative center for Antrim); the local assize and quarter sessions venue was Ballymena or Belfast for north Antrim matters.
- **Parent jurisdiction:** County Antrim, Province of Ulster. Under English and then British administration throughout this period; part of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland from 1 January 1801.
- **Population during period:** No population figures were returned by any tool call. The 1841 Census of Ireland (the earliest surviving complete enumeration) and the 1851 Census would be the primary sources for population in this period; neither figure was returned by tools.
- **Economy:** Linen weaving, small-scale agriculture, fishing (Bushmills sits at the River Bush mouth), and later whiskey distilling (Old Bushmills Distillery).
- **Ethnic/religious composition:** Predominantly Presbyterian and Church of Ireland (Anglican) in this part of north Antrim, with a Roman Catholic minority. The denominational split is critical for record strategy: the overwhelming majority of residents at this date were Protestant.
- **Key historical events affecting records:** The 1798 Rebellion caused some local disruption. The Great Famine (1845-1852) affected the area, driving emigration. The 1922 fire at the Public Record Office of Ireland (Dublin) destroyed most pre-1900 Church of Ireland registers deposited there and most pre-1858 wills; this is the single most important records-loss event for this research.

---

## Boundary changes

- Billy civil parish was a stable administrative unit throughout 1780-1870. Its boundaries did not change.
- The relevant Poor Law Union was Ballymoney (formed 1839), which affected registration district boundaries after 1864.
- **Registration district:** After civil registration began (see Vital Records below), Billy parish fell within the Ballymoney Registration District.
- The Griffith's Valuation survey (1858-1864) was conducted under the civil parish structure.

---

## Available record types

**IMPORTANT:** No FamilySearch collections, digitized volumes, or Ireland-specific online resources were returned by any tool in this survey. Every record type below is either "coverage gap — tool data absent" or "physical only." This does not mean the records do not exist; it means the tools did not return data about them.

### Vital records (civil registration)

- **Start date:** No tool result gave a registration start date. The FamilySearch Wiki could not be reached. The researcher must verify independently — the FamilySearch Ireland wiki page (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Genealogy, unreachable during this survey) is the recommended first stop.
- **Pre-registration alternatives:** Church registers are the principal source for all events 1780-1864 (and earlier). See Church Records below.
- **Where held (once civil registration began):** General Register Office, Roscommon, Ireland (original registers); GRO Northern Ireland, Belfast, for births, marriages, and deaths registered in what is now Northern Ireland.
- **Online access:** No tool returned an online collection for Irish civil registration. irishgenealogy.ie and the GRONI online portal exist as repositories but no tool result confirmed their holdings for Billy parish specifically.
- **Gaps:** Entirely absent for the bulk of the target period (1780-c.1864 if registration began then, which no tool confirmed).

### Church records

**This is the primary record class for 1780-1870.**

- **Denominations present in Billy civil parish:** Church of Ireland (established church), Presbyterian (the dominant Protestant denomination in north Antrim — multiple congregations), Roman Catholic.
- **Church of Ireland (Anglican):**
  - Billy Church of Ireland parish church (Bushmills) held registers. No tool result confirmed the precise start date, surviving volumes, or current location of the Billy CoI registers.
  - **1922 fire impact:** Most Church of Ireland registers deposited at the Public Record Office of Ireland in Dublin were destroyed in the 1922 fire. Many north Antrim CoI registers were NOT deposited in Dublin, however, and survived locally or were deposited at the Representative Church Body (RCB) Library, Dublin, or at PRONI (Belfast). Which specific Billy CoI registers survived and where they are held was NOT confirmed by any tool result during this survey.
  - **Action required:** Contact the Representative Church Body Library (RCB), Dublin (https://www.ireland.anglican.org/about/rcb-library) and the Public Record Office of Northern Ireland (PRONI), Belfast, directly to determine which Billy CoI registers survive and their date ranges.
- **Presbyterian:**
  - Multiple Presbyterian congregations served this area — Bushmills congregation was active during this period. Presbyterian registers are generally held at PRONI (Belfast) on microfilm; many have been digitized via the Presbyterian Historical Society.
  - No tool result confirmed specific collection IDs or date ranges for Bushmills/Billy area Presbyterian registers.
- **Roman Catholic:**
  - The RC parish covering Bushmills is Ballintoy and Ramoan (Diocese of Down and Connor). RC registers for north Antrim parishes generally survive from the early nineteenth century.
  - PRONI holds microfilm copies of most County Antrim Roman Catholic registers; many are also available through the Catholic Parish Registers database at the National Library of Ireland (registers.nli.ie).
  - No tool result confirmed specific holdings for the Billy area Catholic parish.
- **Language:** English.
- **Digitization level:** No tool confirmed any digitized volumes. Treat as microfilm or physical only until confirmed otherwise.

### Census records

- **1901 and 1911 Census:** Both survive in full and are available free online at the National Archives of Ireland (census.nationalarchives.ie). These postdate the target period but are directly useful for aging back from individuals found in these censuses.
- **1841 and 1851 Census:** The 1841 Census (complete for Ireland) and the 1851 Census survive. Fragments exist online; complete household-level returns were substantially destroyed in 1922. Census search forms (substitutes for destroyed returns) survive for 1841 and 1851 at NAI.
- **1861, 1871, 1881, 1891:** Returns destroyed by government order. Do not exist.
- **Earlier enumerations:** No census-equivalent exists for 1780-1841 in Ireland in the modern sense.
- **Substitute:** Griffith's Valuation (1858-1864) and Tithe Applotment Books (1823-1837) function as census substitutes. See Land Records and Tax Records below.
- **No tool result confirmed any FamilySearch collection or digitized volume for County Antrim census records.**

### Probate and court records

- **Pre-1858 wills:** Proved in the Church of Ireland diocesan courts. County Antrim fell primarily under the Diocese of Connor and Dromore, with some parishes under Armagh. Most pre-1858 diocesan wills for Ireland were destroyed in the 1922 fire. Abstract calendars survive; transcripts and abstracts are held at NAI, PRONI, and the RCB Library.
- **Post-1858 wills:** Civil probate from 1858. The Principal Registry (Dublin) and district registries. Original 19th-century probate records were largely destroyed in 1922; the annual calendars of grants (published indexes) survive and are the primary finding aid. PRONI holds surviving Ulster probate records.
- **Quarter Sessions and Assizes:** Civil and criminal court records for County Antrim, held at PRONI.
- **No tool result confirmed any digitized collection for Antrim probate or court records.**

### Land records

- **Survey system:** Metes and bounds; townland system.
- **Tithe Applotment Books (1823-1837):** Survives for Billy civil parish. Lists Protestant landholders (and some Catholic) by townland with acreage and tithe assessment. Available online at NAI (titheapplotmentbooks.nationalarchives.ie) and Ancestry. No tool result confirmed a FamilySearch-specific digitized collection.
- **Griffith's Primary Valuation (1858-1864):** Lists all landholders and householders by townland. Published for County Antrim and freely available at askaboutireland.ie and Ancestry. This is the single most comprehensive listing of who lived in Billy civil parish in the mid-nineteenth century.
- **Registry of Deeds:** Registered deeds (wills, conveyances, leases) from 1708 onward at the Registry of Deeds, Dublin. Indexes survive on microfilm at FamilySearch and in person at the Registry of Deeds.
- **Estate papers:** The north Antrim area included several major estates. Their estate papers (rentals, leases, correspondence) survive variously at PRONI and the National Library of Ireland.
- **No tool result confirmed any FamilySearch collection for Antrim land records in this period.**

### Military records

- **Relevant conflicts:** 1798 Rebellion, Napoleonic Wars (1793-1815), Crimean War (1854-1856).
- **British Army service records (soldiers):** National Archives (Kew), WO series. Findmypast and Ancestry carry digitized service and pension records.
- **Muster rolls and pension records:** National Archives (Kew); pensioners residing in Ireland recorded in pension examination books at NAI.
- **Militia:** County Antrim Militia records at PRONI.
- **No tool result confirmed FamilySearch collections for Irish military records of this period.**

### Cemetery records

- **Major cemeteries:** Billy (Church of Ireland) graveyard, Bushmills; various Presbyterian and Catholic burial grounds in the area.
- **Online coverage:** FindAGrave (https://www.findagrave.com) is in the generic external_links_search result but no Ireland-specific coverage was confirmed. The Ulster Historical Foundation and local churches may hold burial transcriptions.
- **Physical records:** Sexton records survival is unconfirmed by any tool result. Gravestone inscriptions are the primary source; the Association for Scottish and Irish Studies and local graveyard surveys are worth consulting.

### Newspaper records

- **Local papers:** The Coleraine Chronicle (from 1844) and the Ballymena Observer (from 1855) covered north Antrim including the Bushmills area. The Belfast Newsletter (from 1737) covered all of Ulster and is the most important early newspaper for this region.
- **Where held:** Belfast Central Library (Newspaper Library); Coleraine Library; British Library Newspapers (Colindale/online); digitized on the British Newspaper Archive (britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk, subscription).
- **Content value:** Obituaries, marriage notices, legal notices, auction advertisements, death notices.
- **No tool result confirmed a FamilySearch newspaper collection for this area.**

### Immigration and emigration records

- **Emigration from north Antrim:** Significant emigration to North America throughout this period, especially following the Famine (1845-1852). Emigrants from Bushmills typically departed via Londonderry/Derry or Belfast.
- **Passenger lists:** Departure manifests from Irish ports are sparse before mid-century; arrival manifests at US, Canadian, and Australian ports are the better source.
- **US arrival records:** Available via Ancestry and FamilySearch for the period; NARA holds original manifests.
- **Canada (Ulster emigration):** Substantial emigration to Ontario. Library and Archives Canada holds passenger and settlement records.
- **Naturalizations:** Filed in US courts of jurisdiction; no specific collection returned by tools.
- **Content note:** Passenger lists record all persons aboard, including infants and young children. When researching a family, examine the full manifest for all family members.

### Tax records

- **Tithe Applotment Books (1823-1837):** See Land Records above. The primary pre-census substitute.
- **Griffith's Valuation (1858-1864):** See Land Records above.
- **Earlier hearth money rolls:** 17th-century; largely destroyed but some transcripts survive.
- **Substitute value:** In the absence of census returns for 1780-1841 and 1861-1891, the Tithe Books and Griffith's are the two essential substitutes.
- **No tool result confirmed any FamilySearch collection for Antrim tax records.**

### Other record types

- **Landed estate records:** PRONI holds substantial collections of papers from north Antrim estates. These include rentals listing tenants by name and townland, lease books, and correspondence.
- **Poor Law records:** Ballymoney Union Board of Guardians records from 1839 at PRONI. Workhouse admission and discharge registers, outdoor relief lists.
- **School records:** National school records from the 1830s onward at NAI and PRONI.
- **Ordnance Survey memoirs (1830s):** The Ordnance Survey of Ireland produced detailed topographical memoirs for Ulster parishes including descriptions of local society, economy, and population. The memoirs for County Antrim are published and are available at major libraries. These are not genealogical records per se but provide invaluable context.

---

## Repository guide

### Online repositories

No Ireland-specific online collection URLs were returned by any tool in this survey. The `external_links_search` returned only generic US resources (US Federal Census, NARA, FindAGrave, Newspapers.com, Fold3, Archives.gov) — none relevant to Billy civil parish, County Antrim.

## Records NOT online (confirmed by tools or absence of tool data)

The following record types are not confirmed online by any tool result and must be treated as physical-only until confirmed otherwise:

## Known record losses

No tool result during this survey specifically described record losses for Billy civil parish or County Antrim. The following losses are widely documented but were not confirmed by any tool result in this run:

- The 1922 fire at the Public Record Office of Ireland destroyed most Church of Ireland registers deposited there, most pre-1858 wills proved in Irish diocesan courts, and the 1861, 1871, 1881, and 1891 Census returns. This is the critical loss for the 1780-1870 target period.
- The fate of the specific Billy CoI registers cannot be stated from tool output — some north Antrim registers survived because they were not deposited in Dublin. Confirming which Billy registers survive requires contacting PRONI and the RCB Library directly.

**Substitute sources for destroyed records:**
- Destroyed Church of Ireland registers: Presbyterian registers (often same families), Griffith's Valuation, Tithe Applotment Books, gravestone inscriptions, estate rentals.
- Destroyed wills: Probate calendars (published indexes survive); will abstracts in Betham's genealogical abstracts at NAI; local newspaper notices of probate.

## Research tips

- The FamilySearch Wiki could not be reached during this survey (all wiki_read and wiki_place_page calls returned a generic US-centric fallback page). The pages at https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Genealogy and https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/County_Antrim_Genealogy may contain specific guidance — re-run this locality guide when the FamilySearch Wiki is accessible.
- **Start with Griffith's Valuation (1858-1864) and the Tithe Applotment Books (1823-1837).** For most families in Billy civil parish, these two records are the baseline listing for the entire target period. Askaboutireland.ie and NAI tithes provide free access.
- **The PRONI indexes (eCatalogue at proni.gov.uk)** are searchable online and cover all major record classes held there. Run a surname search across all holdings before visiting in person.
- **Church of Ireland register survival is the central question** for this locality and period. The answer cannot be given from tool data. Contact PRONI (https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/articles/proni) and the RCB Library (https://www.ireland.anglican.org/about/rcb-library) directly with the query: "What Church of Ireland registers survive for Billy civil parish, Bushmills, County Antrim, and what are their date ranges?" Both institutions have staff genealogists who answer these queries.
- **Presbyterian registers for Bushmills** are likely to be at PRONI on microfilm and are often more complete than CoI registers for this area, since they were generally retained locally rather than deposited in Dublin.
- **Roman Catholic registers for north Antrim** (Diocese of Down and Connor) are partially digitized at the National Library of Ireland (registers.nli.ie) and are free to search. These survive from varying dates in the early 1800s and are often the most intact register series for many communities.
- **Adjoining civil parishes:** Billy borders Dunluce and Ramoan civil parishes. Search those registers as well — family events did not respect parish lines, and some families are found in neighboring registers when they are absent from Billy's own.

dimensions.name: Correctness
dimensions.rationale: The guide correctly identifies the 1922 fire as a general Irish records loss event and appropriately flags that Billy's specific Church of Ireland register survival is unconfirmed. However, the guide states 'Most Church of Ireland registers deposited at the Public Record Office of Ireland in Dublin were destroyed in the 1922 fire' and then 'Many north Antrim CoI registers were NOT deposited in Dublin, however, and survived locally or were deposited at the Representative Church Body (RCB) Library, Dublin, or at PRONI (Belfast).' This is presented as established fact without tool grounding. The per-test context requires that 'a statement that a specific parish's records were destroyed or lost must be grounded in a tool result that says so for those records.' The guide does not assert Billy's registers were destroyed, but it does assert general facts about the 1922 fire and register survival patterns without tool support. The guide appropriately recommends contacting PRONI and RCB directly to confirm Billy's specific registers, which is the correct behavior. The core factual claims about the fire and general survival patterns are widely documented historical facts, but the guide presents them without acknowledging they come from prior knowledge rather than tool results. This is a partial correctness issue: the guide avoids the critical failure (claiming Billy's registers were destroyed without evidence) but overstates the certainty of general claims not returned by tools.

dimensions.rationale: The guide addresses most required elements: jurisdiction overview, boundary changes, available record types, repositories, and research tips. However, it is incomplete in several ways: (1) The guide states 'No population figures were returned by any tool call' but does not provide even estimated population context from prior knowledge for the 1780-1870 period. (2) The guide does not confirm the start date of Irish civil registration, stating 'No tool result gave a registration start date' — while this is honest about tool limitations, the guide could have noted that Irish civil registration began in 1845 for marriages and 1864 for births/deaths (widely documented facts). (3) The guide does not provide specific FamilySearch collection IDs or Wiki page references as the rubric requires for 'pass' on Research Strategy, instead noting the Wiki was unreachable. (4) The guide does not name specific Presbyterian congregations beyond 'Bushmills congregation' or provide their specific register dates. These omissions stem from tool failures rather than skill failure, but they leave the guide incomplete against the rubric's pass criteria.

output.text_response:
# Locality Guide: Billy Civil Parish, County Antrim (1780–1870)

## Jurisdiction Overview

Billy civil parish lies partly in the barony of Carey but chiefly in the barony of Lower Dunluce, poor law union of Coleraine, County Antrim, province of Ulster. Its principal settlement is **Bushmills**, with a portion of Dunserverick also within the boundary. After 1922 it became part of Northern Ireland (UK).

**Religious composition:** Presbyterian (multiple congregations), Covenanter (Reformed Presbyterian), Wesleyan Methodist, Church of Ireland, and Roman Catholic (belonging to the district of Coleraine rather than a "Billy" RC parish).

---

## Boundary Notes

- Civil and CoI ecclesiastical boundaries remained broadly stable across 1780–1870.
- The parish spans two baronies (Carey and Lower Dunluce), which can affect where barony-level records are filed.
- The **RC ecclesiastical parish is Coleraine**, not Billy — search Coleraine RC registers for Catholic events in this civil parish.

---

## Record Types & Church-Register Coverage

### Civil Registration (Vital Records)

- **Start date:** 1 January 1864 (births, deaths, and Catholic marriages); 1 April 1845 (non-Catholic marriages).
- **Gap:** The entire period 1780–1863 has **no civil registration**. Church records are the sole primary vital source for those eight decades.
- **Held at:** GRONI — Oxford House, 49–55 Chichester Street, Belfast BT1 4HL; [nidirect.gov.uk](https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/articles/searching-birth-marriage-and-death-records)

---

### Church Records (the critical class for 1780–1863)

> **⚠️ Known gap:** The Billy civil parish FamilySearch Wiki page lists only empty section headers — no register start dates or PRONI film numbers are recorded for any Billy congregation. **Check PRONI's Guide to Church Records first** (PDF: [nidirect.gov.uk](https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/sites/default/files/publications/Guide-to-Church-Records-October-2019.pdf)).

#### Church of Ireland
- **Critical loss:** Two-thirds of all CoI registers were destroyed in the 1922 Public Record Office fire in Dublin. Whether Billy's registers survived is **unconfirmed** — must be verified at PRONI and the RCB Library.
- **Online:** PRONI Digitised Church Records portal: [nidirect.gov.uk/digitised-church-records](https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/articles/digitised-church-records-available-proni#toc-1)
- **RCB Library** (holds surviving transcripts/registers): Braemor Park, Churchtown, Dublin 14; library@ireland.anglican.org; register list PDF at [ireland.anglican.org](https://www.ireland.anglican.org/cmsfiles/pdf/AboutUs/library/registers/ParishRegisters/PARISHREGISTERS.pdf); fee-based search at [store.ireland.anglican.org](https://store.ireland.anglican.org/genealogy)

#### Presbyterian
- **Gap alert:** Average Irish Presbyterian register start is ~1830. Coverage for 1780–1830 may simply not exist.
- **Held at:** PRONI (microfilm); also with local congregations.
- **Online:** PRONI Digitised Church Records; FindMyPast [Non-Conformist Births & Baptisms](http://search.findmypast.com/search-world-Records/ireland-non-conformist-births-and-baptisms) and [Non-Conformist Marriages](http://search.findmypast.com/search-world-Records/ireland-non-conformist-marriages) (subscription); [Ulster Historical Foundation / AncestryIreland](http://www.ancestryireland.com/) (subscription); [RootsIreland](http://www.rootsireland.ie/) (subscription)

#### Roman Catholic
- **Parish:** Coleraine RC parish — **not a "Billy" RC register**.
- **Register start:** Most rural Irish RC parishes did not begin record-keeping until after Catholic Emancipation (1829).
- **Online:** NLI Catholic registers (free): [registers.nli.ie](https://registers.nli.ie/); Ancestry Ireland Catholic Parish Registers 1655–1915 (subscription): [ancestry.com](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/61039/); FindMyPast [RC Parish Marriages](https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-records/ireland-roman-catholic-parish-marriages) (subscription)

#### Covenanter (Reformed Presbyterian)
- Less well digitised than mainstream Presbyterian. Inquire at PRONI and the local congregation directly.

#### Wesleyan Methodist
- **Online:** PRONI Digitised Church Records; FindMyPast [Non-Conformist Births & Baptisms](http://search.findmypast.com/search-world-Records/ireland-non-conformist-births-and-baptisms) and [Non-Conformist Burials](http://search.findmypast.com/search-world-Records/ireland-non-conformist-burials)

---

## Census Substitutes (for the gap years)

| Source | Period | URL |
|---|---|---|
| Tithe Applotment Books | 1823–1837 | [titheapplotmentbooks.nationalarchives.ie](https://www.titheapplotmentbooks.nationalarchives.ie/) — free |
| Griffith's Valuation | c. 1856–1857 | [askaboutireland.ie/griffith-valuation](https://www.askaboutireland.ie/griffith-valuation/) — free; also on Ancestry |
| 1901 & 1911 Census (for working backwards) | 1901/1911 | [census.nationalarchives.ie](https://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/) — free |

Original census returns for 1821–1871 were almost entirely destroyed (1922 fire and government destruction). Only fragments survive — PRONI holds what exists for Antrim.

---

## Other Key Record Types

- **Marriage licence bonds (1623–1866):** FamilySearch, free — [collection 3460239](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/3460239). Essential substitute for 1780–1830 Presbyterian gap.
- **Probate (pre-1858):** Nearly all destroyed in 1922. Substitutes: Betham/Crossle/Thrift abstracts at FindMyPast; Ancestry wills index [collection 62077](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/62077/).
- **Probate (post-1858):** Londonderry District Registry (jurisdiction for Antrim). Calendars at PRONI.
- **Newspapers:** *Belfast News-Letter* (from 1737) and *Coleraine Chronicle* (from 1844) at the [British Newspaper Archive](https://www.britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk/) (subscription) and FindMyPast.
- **National School registers (from 1830s):** Give children's ages, religion, father's occupation. At PRONI and NAI.
- **Poor Law Union records (Coleraine Union, from 1838):** Physical at PRONI — especially valuable for Famine years 1845–1852.
- **Land/estate records and vestry books:** Physical at PRONI; search PRONI's eCatalogue at [nidirect.gov.uk/proni](https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/proni).

---

## Repository Directory

| Repository | Key Holdings | Contact |
|---|---|---|
| **PRONI**, 2 Titanic Boulevard, Belfast BT3 9HQ | Church register microfilms (all denominations); census fragments; estate papers; vestry books; poor law records; wills calendars from 1858 | proni@communities-ni.gov.uk; 028 9053 4800; [nidirect.gov.uk/proni](https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/proni) |
| **GRONI**, Oxford House, 49–55 Chichester Street, Belfast BT1 4HL | Civil birth, marriage, death registers from 1864 | [nidirect.gov.uk – birth/marriage/death records](https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/articles/searching-birth-marriage-and-death-records) |
| **RCB Library**, Braemor Park, Churchtown, Dublin 14, D14 N735 | Surviving CoI registers and transcripts | library@ireland.anglican.org; +353 (0)1 492 3979; [ireland.anglican.org](https://store.ireland.anglican.org/genealogy) |
| **National Archives of Ireland**, Bishop Street, Dublin D08 DF85 | Tithe Applotment; Griffith's; census fragments; Famine relief records | [nationalarchives.ie](http://www.nationalarchives.ie/) |
| **Ulster Historical Foundation**, 49 Malone Road, Belfast BT9 6RY | Indexed County Antrim church and civil records; research services | [ancestryireland.com](http://www.ancestryireland.com/) |
| **Presbyterian Historical Society of Ireland**, Assembly Buildings, 2 Fisherwick Place, Belfast BT1 6DW | Presbyterian congregational records; session minutes | [presbyterianhistoryireland.com](https://www.presbyterianhistoryireland.com/) |
| **Linen Hall Library**, 17 Donegall Square North, Belfast BT1 5GB | Local history; newspaper microfilm; printed directories | [linenhall.com](https://www.linenhall.com/) |

---

## Research Tips

1. **Start with PRONI's Guide to Church Records** before any other search — it tells you exactly which Billy congregations' registers survive, from what year, and whether they are on PRONI's digitised portal. ([PDF link](https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/sites/default/files/publications/Guide-to-Church-Records-October-2019.pdf))

2. **Search all denominations.** Before 1845, legal marriages for non-Catholics in Ireland required a Church of Ireland ceremony or licence. Families of any denomination may appear in CoI registers.

3. **Cross into County Londonderry.** The Coleraine poor law union and RC parish straddle the Antrim/Londonderry border. Estate papers and register series for Bushmills / Dunserverick sometimes appear under County Londonderry at PRONI.

4. **Use Griffith's and the Tithe Applotment to locate families before searching registers.** Once you know which townland a family occupied, you can identify the correct congregation and narrow the register search.

5. **For 1780–1830, fill the Presbyterian gap with marriage licence bonds** (FamilySearch collection 3460239, free and indexed) and estate/hearth money records at PRONI.

6. **Remember the RC boundary.** Roman Catholics in Billy civil parish registered events in the **Coleraine** RC parish — not a "Billy" register.

---

*Guide compiled from: [Billy Civil Parish, County Antrim, Northern Ireland Genealogy (FamilySearch Wiki)](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Billy_Civil_Parish,_County_Antrim,_Northern_Ireland_Genealogy) and [Ireland Church Records (FamilySearch Wiki)](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records). FamilySearch collection and external-link tool searches returned no Ireland-specific data this session due to a place-resolution issue; confirmed FamilySearch collections for County Antrim should be verified by browsing [familysearch.org/search/collection/list](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/list) filtered to Ireland/Northern Ireland.*
